title: Checks for unused imports.
summary: Unused imports add a performance overhead at runtime, and risk creating import cycles. They also increase the cognitive load of reading the code. Ruff takes this rule from Pyflakes and made it stable in v0.0.18.
message_templates: `{}` imported but unused; consider using `importlib.util.find_spec` to test for availability
`{}` imported but unused; consider removing, adding to `__all__`, or using a redundant alias

title: Checks for import bindings that are shadowed by loop variables.
summary: Shadowing an import with loop variables makes the code harder to read and reason about, as the identify of the imported binding is no longer clear. It's also often indicative of a mistake, as it's unlikely that the loop variable is intended to be used as the imported binding. Ruff takes this rule from Pyflakes and made it stable in v0.0.44.
message_templates: Import `{}` from {} shadowed by loop variable

title: Checks for the use of wildcard imports.
summary: Wildcard imports (e.g., from module import *) make it hard to determine which symbols are available in the current namespace, and from which module they were imported. They're also discouraged by PEP 8. Ruff takes this rule from Pyflakes and made it stable in v0.0.18.
message_templates: `from {} import *` used; unable to detect undefined names

title: Checks for __future__ imports that are not located at the beginning of a file.
summary: Imports from __future__ must be placed the beginning of the file, before any other statements (apart from docstrings). The use of __future__ imports elsewhere is invalid and will result in a SyntaxError. Ruff takes this rule from Pyflakes and made it stable in v0.0.34.
message_templates: `from __future__` imports must occur at the beginning of the file

title: Checks for names that might be undefined, but may also be defined in a wildcard import.
summary: Wildcard imports (e.g., from module import *) make it hard to determine which symbols are available in the current namespace. If a module contains a wildcard import, and a name in the current namespace has not been explicitly defined or imported, then it's unclear whether the name is undefined or was imported by the wildcard import. Ruff takes this rule from Pyflakes and made it stable in v0.0.44.
message_templates: `{}` may be undefined, or defined from star imports

title: Check for the use of wildcard imports outside of the module namespace.
summary: The use of wildcard imports outside of the module namespace (e.g., within functions) can lead to confusion, as the import can shadow local variables. Ruff takes this rule from Pyflakes and made it stable in v0.0.37.
message_templates: `from {} import *` only allowed at module level

title: Checks for __future__ imports that are not defined in the current Python version.
summary: Importing undefined or unsupported members from the __future__ module is a SyntaxError. Ruff takes this rule from Pyflakes and made it stable in v0.0.34.
